chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abu Harun al-Makfuf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

To Abu Harun al-Makfuf: O Abu Harun! We command our children to recite the Tasbih of al-Zahra (peace be upon her) just as we command them to offer Salat. So adhere to it, for no servant recites it and becomes unfortunate.

key_terms.الْمَكْفُوفِ: The blind (epithet of the narrator Abu Harun)
key_terms.تَسْبِيحِ الزَّهْرَاءِ: The specific litany of praises attributed to Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of reciting Tasbih al-Zahra according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs Abu Harun al-Makfuf to consistently recite the Tasbih of Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her), equating its importance in his household to that of the daily prayers. He emphasizes that adherence to this specific dhikr ensures prosperity and prevents misfortune for the believer. This narration highlights the unique status of Fatima al-Zahra in Shia tradition, where her supplications are viewed as a means of spiritual protection and divine favor, often linked to the intercession of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) told Abu Haroon Makfuf, “O Abu Haroon! We advise our children to recite Tasbih of Zahra (s.a.) much in the same way as we do to offer Salaat. You too  recite  this  Tasbih  for  one  who  does  not  recite  it,  is unfortunate.”
